record.paper_title: A survey of equivariant map algebras with open problems
record.original_question: Let k be an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, let X be an affine scheme over k, let g be a finite-dimensional Lie algebra over k, let Γ act on X and g by automorphisms, and set M = M(X,g)^Γ, the Γ-fixed equivariant map Lie algebra. Compute the higher Ext groups between finite-dimensional M-modules, explain how these Ext groups interact with both the representation theory of g and the geometry of X, and determine how the global dimension of the finite-dimensional M-module category is governed by that geometry.

evidence.quote: The action of Γ on X induces an action on the coordinate ring A of X. Then M = (a ⊗ A)Γ , the fixed points of the diagonal action of Γ on a ⊗ A.

(a) Higher extensions. Only the first Ext groups are calculated in [NS], where it is shown that these groups are related to both the representation theory of the target g and the geometry of the scheme X (see, for instance, Proposition 3.5, which involves the tangent space). It is natural to try to compute higher Ext groups. One would expect a rich interplay between these groups and the geometry of the scheme X. It would be particularly interesting to see how the global dimension of the category of finite-dimensional modules is related to this geometry.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, let $X$ be an affine scheme over $k$ with coordinate ring $A$, let $\mathfrak{g}$ be a finite-dimensional Lie algebra over $k$, and let $\Gamma$ be a group acting on $X$ (equivalently on $A$) and on $\mathfrak{g}$ by automorphisms. Define the equivariant map Lie algebra
$$M = M(X,\mathfrak{g})^{\Gamma} = (\mathfrak{g} \otimes_k A)^{\Gamma},$$
the subalgebra of $\Gamma$-fixed points of the diagonal action of $\Gamma$ on $\mathfrak{g} \otimes_k A$, with Lie bracket induced from $\mathfrak{g}$ and the commutative multiplication on $A$.

(a) For finite-dimensional $M$-modules $V$ and $W$, compute the higher extension groups $\operatorname{Ext}^n_M(V,W)$ for all $n \geq 1$.

(b) Describe explicitly how these $\operatorname{Ext}^n$-groups depend on, and interact with, both the representation theory of $\mathfrak{g}$ and the geometry of the scheme $X$ (for instance, via local invariants such as tangent spaces at $\Gamma$-orbits of points of $X$).

(c) Determine the global dimension of the category of finite-dimensional $M$-modules, and express this global dimension in terms of geometric invariants of $X$ (and the $\Gamma$-action).
artifact.status_search_result: The literature on equivariant map algebras and related twisted current algebras has computed $\operatorname{Ext}^1$ between finite-dimensional simple modules and used these computations for block decompositions and extension-locality results (Neher–Savage; Kodera; Lau and others). However, available sources do not provide a general computation of higher $\operatorname{Ext}^n$ ($n\geq 2$) between finite-dimensional $M$-modules, nor a determination of the global dimension of the finite-dimensional module category in terms of the geometry of $X$. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Extensions and block decompositions for finite-dimensional representations of equivariant map algebras
status_evidence.snippet: Describes Ext^1 between irreducible finite-dimensional representations of equivariant map algebras.

status_evidence.title: Extensions of modules for twisted current algebras
status_evidence.snippet: Studies extensions between finite-dimensional simple modules for twisted current algebras and proves extension-locality.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent work continues to focus on first extensions, not higher Ext groups or global dimension.

status_evidence.title: A survey of equivariant map algebras with open problems
status_evidence.snippet: Only the first Ext groups are calculated... It is natural to try to compute higher Ext groups... see how the global dimension of the category of finite-dimensional modules is related to this geometry.
status_evidence.claim: The computation of higher Ext groups and the global dimension is stated as an open problem.
